report.clinical_summary: The patient has Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL) that is progressing slowly. They are in the watchful waiting phase with monthly blood monitoring. They experience fatigue and night sweats that affect their work and social life, along with a persistent but not severe swollen neck. They are more prone to minor infections that take longer to heal. They understand the basics of CLL and the progression indicators but feel confused about some aspects. They actively manage through lifestyle changes (exercise, healthy eating, social connections) and seek reassurance about their condition. They have no current medication but understand treatment will eventually be needed.
